content:
Hi,
On https://github.com/PerAlexandersson/RealRooted there is a larger repo with classical results in algebraic combinatorics. The famous result that independence polynomials of claw-free graps are real-rooted is fully formalized as well as many other results, Eulerian polynomials, Narayana polynomials, as well as theorems about interlacing roots, operators etc.
Hi @Per Alexandersson ! Can you say something about AI being used/not used for something in the project?
Everything is LLM-generated, but @Erik (√2) and I are slowly cleaning the material up to mathlib standards

Right, i use AI a lot, since im new to lean. The theorems being formalized are chosen to be useful for future proofs, and i have successfully managed to get some research results formalized on top of this library. I'll learn more lean i hope, and i also guess AI will become better at writing good lean code.

This is kind of part of a larger project, the background is collected and referenced on symmetricfunctions.com, and i have some rust tools as well for actual computations and checking properties. So, the ecosystem is rather well-developed.

I can give pointers and explain the theory if needed. This area is in some sense easy to get into, its basically 'just' polynomials. No tricky abstract concepts. But the theory has been very successful for various nice results and applications
Oh, i should say the latest addition is a tactics, for streamlining lots of boilerplate

Thanks for your openness @Per Alexandersson . Can I say that I don't understand the sentence "A use AI a lot _since_ I'm new to Lean"? In the sense that if you're not very much into formal methods/type theory/proof assistants, why making all this work? And on the other hand, if you like them, why not spending your time studying Mathematics in Lean (for example) insteas? It's a honest question, really, I'm trying to understand new motivations that drive contributions and were not around before AI.

@Filippo A. E. Nuccio that is a fair question! So, i want to verify proofs im actually working on. Some proofs are also AI produced, but the proofs that are AI generated are usually flawed. So formalizing them is an absolutely required step.

The repo contais lots of standard tools, that many people in this field would find useful, so its different from say formalizing just one famous result.

I totally understand the aversion towards AI, but i find it useful to have something to start with, and then massage it to what we actually want.

Sure, sure, thanks! I've no aversion towards AI in general, I'm really just trying to understand the trend that motivates people. On the long run, I'm convinced that even more than understanding how AI can be useful (which will be, and hugely) we need to understand how it makes people interact differently with our discipline. So I'm grateful that you took the time to answer in detail! :pray:
